claim: You get a notice for a settlement meeting, in your own city (on-screen: LOK ADALAT · YOUR CITY)

'Your own city' is the usual case, not a rule: a pre-litigation matter goes to the Lok Adalat for a court that has jurisdiction, which is normally where the borrower lives. claim: In 2026, in a loan case, the Kerala High Court said a bank's hold is not a court attachment, so the usual salary protection doesn't stop it (on-screen tag: [KERALA HIGH COURT | 2026])

claim: Set-off is limited: only your money, only for your debt, only in that bank, only up to what you owe; a bank where you owe nothing cannot touch your account (on-screen: UP TO WHAT YOU OWE · SAME BANK ONLY)

note: Also Kerala HC (CP-124) on set-off: 'As mutuality is essential to the validity of a set-off'; Madras HC, Balaji S v Banking Ombudsman, 2025: lien 'cannot be exercised in case the other loan is not by the same person' (research_rules_C C1.3). 'Up to what you owe': HDFC clause adjusts 'towards dues under the Card Account'. CAVEATS: (1) HDFC's clause also names 'Add-on Cardmember' money, so a family member holding an add-on card on your account may be exposed (optional VO: 'Only your money, and at some banks an add-on card holder's'); (2) a hold can freeze the whole account while the bank adjusts (Kerala case: the salary account was frozen); (3) a court order in a case can still attach accounts (see C081 row).

claim: The bank does not have to tell you before it puts the hold ('Not before')

The rule continues in the RBI (Commercial Banks – IRACP) Directions 2025, para 44 'Asset classification shall be borrower-wise and not facility-wise' (TaxGuru copy, research_rules_C C3.1). Applies to banks; an NBFC issuer such as SBI Card is a separate lender.

note: RBI/2022-23/108, DOR.ORG.REC.65/21.04.158/2022-23, 12 Aug 2022 (page opened 2026-10-12); listed among practices REs and agents must not resort to. Same window in the new rule from 1 Jan 2027 (RBI/2026-27/223 para 454Y(4), research_rules_B B1.1). Status note: these circulars appear to have been folded into RBI's consolidated Commercial Banks (Responsible Business Conduct) Directions 2025, whose recovery-agent part the August 2026 Fourth Amendment replaces from 1 Jan 2027 (search summary, not opened); the rule itself is unchanged. Optional tag: [RBI | RECOVERY AGENT RULES].

claim: No threats, no abuse, no calls to shame your family or friends
source_quote: do not resort to intimidation or harassment of any kind, either verbal or physical, against any person in their debt collection efforts, including acts intended to humiliate publicly or intrude upon the privacy of the debtors' family members, referees and friends, sending inappropriate messages either on mobile or through social media, making threatening and/ or anonymous calls
note: RBI 12 Aug 2022 circular, para 2.

claim: Anyone who comes home must show an ID card and the bank's authorisation letter (on-screen: ID + BANK LETTER [RBI | 2008 & 2022 CIRCULARS])
source_quote: it would be appropriate if the agent also carries a copy of the notice and the authorization letter from the bank along with the identity card issued to him by the bank or the agency firm / company.
note: RBI/2007-2008/296, 24 Apr 2008 (page opened). Banks' customer code: the person 'will identify himself / herself and produce the authority letter issued by us and upon request show you his / her identity card' (BCSBI Code 2018, IndusInd copy). From 1 Jan 2027 agents must display the ID card (RBI/2026-27/223 para 454X). The 2008 text says 'carries'; optional precise VO: 'must carry an ID card and the bank's authorisation letter. Ask to see them.'

claim: Complain to the bank first; no answer in thirty days, go to the RBI Ombudsman on the RBI complaint website; it is free; since July 2026 you have only ninety days; RBI helpline 14448 (on-screen: CMS.RBI.ORG.IN · 90 DAYS · 14448 [RBI | OMBUDSMAN SCHEME 2026])
source_quote: The complaint must be made to the RBI Ombudsman within 90 days from the date on which the above timeline expires or the date of the last communication from the concerned Regulated Entity, whichever is later.
note: RBI FAQ on RB-IOS 2026 (opened 2026-10-12): 'It comes into force with effect from July 1, 2026. RB-IOS, 2026 replaces the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021.'; 'The complainant must first approach the concerned Regulated Entity' ... 'not received any reply within 30 days'; 'There is no charge or fee for filing or resolving complaints under RB-IOS, 2026.'; portal 'https://cms.rbi.org.in'; 'The IVRS facility on Toll Free No. 14448 is available 24x7.' The helpline gives information and status; complaints are filed online, by email or post. Tag right.

claim: If someone threatens you, call 112; for a fake link or a fake notice, call 1930 (on-screen: 112 · 1930)
source_quote: a nationwide, unified emergency response system with a single emergency number '112', for reporting and addressing all kinds of emergencies from across the country.
note: MHA ERSS page (opened 2026-10-12). 1930: Kerala Police (Ernakulam Rural Cyber PS), 3 Aug 2023, 'National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline No 1930' ... 'The helpline number 1930 is available 24 hours a day.'; cybercrime.gov.in 'allows direct reporting of online crimes, including financial frauds' (WebFetch; page TLS certificate expired). Amar Ujala 16 May 2026 gives 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in for fake summons messages (research_rules_B B3.2). 1930 is mainly for money lost to online fraud; optional on-screen add: CYBERCRIME.GOV.IN.

claim: A lawyer's notice is not a court summons; a real court case has a case number you can type yourself on the eCourts website; never tap the link in the message (on-screen: 3 · CHECK THE CASE NUMBER YOURSELF [ECOURTS])
source_quote: Enter the 16 digit alphanumeric CNR Number without any hyphen or space Click Search button to view current status and history of the case If you don't know the CNR number of the case, click on the Case Status icon on the left menu to search the case with other options like case registration number, party name, advocate name etc.
note: eCourts Services page opened 2026-10-12. Legal notice vs summons: a summons is issued by a court and signed by its presiding officer (BNSS s.63, courtbook.in) while a legal notice is drafted by an advocate for the client (leadindia.law), research_rules_B B3.1. eCourts covers district and high courts; DRT, consumer commission and arbitration matters are not on it (they have their own portals), so the advice fits court cases, as the VO says.

claim: Step four: if you settle, settle on paper; get the settlement letter from the bank first; pay only through the bank's own channel; never cash to an agent (on-screen: 4 · LETTER FIRST · NEVER CASH)
source_quote: any negotiated arrangement with the borrower to fully settle the claims of the RE against the borrower in cash
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION (advice, framed as a practical step). Support: under the RBI June 2023 framework a settlement must be approved by a named authority, so an agent's phone promise is not a sanctioned settlement (inference); real dispute where a bank demanded more after accepting part payment (Anil Kumar v Axis Bank, Bathinda, 2024, research_practical 5.4, PARTLY).

claim: After a settlement your CIBIL will say settled, not closed
source_quote: There are four different status of accounts under this section; Open, Closed, Settled and Written Off.
note: Experian India (MD Ashish Singhal), July 2019: 'If you find 'Settled' against any account, it means that you have entered into a negotiation with the lender'; 'Live and closed loans have a positive impact on your credit score, as long as you have made all the payments regularly.' SBI Card FAQ separates 'settled' and clean-up (CP-153). On-screen DOODLE 'SETTLED → CLOSED' with a question mark matches.

claim: After a settlement that bank won't lend to you for at least a year (on-screen tag: [RBI | JUNE 2023])
source_quote: (i) The cooling period in respect of exposures other than farm credit exposures shall be subject to a floor of 12 months. REs are free to stipulate higher cooling periods in terms of their Board approved policies.
note: RBI 8 June 2023 framework, para 11: cooling period 'before the REs can assume fresh exposures to such borrowers'. Binds the settling lender only; other lenders decide from your report.

claim: Later, ask the bank what you must pay to clean that record (on-screen tag: [SBI CARD | FAQ])
source_quote: In case your account is settled, please call us to know the process and the amount payable for CIBIL status clean up.
note: SBI Card FAQ opened 2026-10-12; clean-up 'may take 45-60 days post realization of funds'. Other banks' policies not checked; the VO's 'ask the bank' is the right framing.

claim: Step five (opinion): with many cards, pay first the bank where your salary sits, next the small bills, then the rest (on-screen: 5 · OUR SUGGESTED ORDER)
source_quote: It is agreed that the Bank, at any time and without notice, will have a lien and right of set-off on all monies belonging to the Cardmember
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION, labelled on screen (OUR SUGGESTED ORDER) and in the VO ('This is my practical view, not a rule'). Reasons are sourced: set-off at the salary bank (CP-122) and fees hitting small bills hardest (CP-155).

claim: Fees grow small bills fastest
note: HDFC MITC 'Version 4.14 Dated October 2026', late payment charges table (excl. GST). ₹750 is 7.5% of a ₹10,000 balance; ₹1,300 is at most 2.6% of any balance above ₹50,000 and 1.3% of ₹1 lakh (our arithmetic). ICICI, SBI Card and Axis use similar slabs (research_practical 6). Interest is the same 3.75% a month at the four big issuers, so the late fee is what separates them.

claim: You can choose where your salary goes; the debt doesn't go away; use the breathing space to settle, not to run
source_quote: without involving any waiver of claims against the borrower, and without prejudice to the recovery of the same.
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION (advice). 'The debt doesn't go away' is sourced (RBI 2023, CP-140). 'You can choose where your salary goes': no rule found either way; most employers pay into an account you name, some insist on a tie-up bank; optional 'You can usually ask your office to pay your salary into another bank.'

claim: Recap: they cannot arrest you just for being unable to pay
source_quote: The mere inability of the appellant to return the loan amount cannot give rise to a criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction
note: Same basis as CP-133; the 'just' keeps the C066 exceptions.

claim: Recap: can they take your salary? Only that same bank, and only up to what you owe
source_quote: salary to the extent of the first one thousand rupees and two third of the remainder in execution of any decree other than a decree for maintenance
note: Incomplete in a way that misleads: it is true for the bank acting on its own (set-off, CP-122/125), but any lender that gets a court decree can have part of your salary attached through the court wherever it is paid: CPC s.60(1)(i), quoted in the Kerala HC judgment, protects only the first ₹1,000 and two-thirds of the rest. A Lok Adalat award is itself a decree (CP-107), and C051 says court cases happen for big dues. FIX: 'Can they take your salary? Without a court order, only that same bank, and only up to what you owe.' | Script fixed 2026-10-12: C081 now says "Without a court order, only that same bank, and only up to what you owe" (court decrees can attach salary under CPC s.60).

claim: Recap: whether they come home depends on how much you owe and where you live
source_quote: The stage of delinquency and the amount at risk will largely determine the specific collection strategy.
note: OUR ESTIMATE / OPINION, the slab-walk conclusion; labelled once CP-113 adds OUR ESTIMATE to the slab walk. 'Where you live': field agencies are listed by city (OneCard agency list; RBL 'Assignment logic will be done based on strategy considering area, coverage etc.').
